question: What does the Act say about discrimination?

answer_full:
The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act outlaws discrimination on the basis of one’s physical, mental or sensory impairment [Factsheet general]. The Act outlaws discrimination in its totality and under any manner or circumstance, and a civil action may be brought by the person discriminated against [Factsheet Section 2].

The Act describes a person with disabilities as one who has a long term physical, mental or sensory impairment that may hinder full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others [Factsheet Section 2].

Section 1(1) of the Act prohibits the discrimination of a person on the ground of his/her disability [Factsheet Section 1]. A person with disability shall not be discriminated against on the ground of his disability [Act cl. 1].

A body corporate who discriminates on this ground is subject to a fine of N1,000,000 while an individual is liable to pay a N100,000 fine, face a six months imprisonment term or both, under section 1(2) [Factsheet Section 1]. A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N1,000,000 if the person is a body corporate [Act cl. 1]. If the person is an individual, they are liable to a fine of N100,000 or six months imprisonment [Act cl. 1].

question: Are public buildings required to be accessible?
answer_excerpt: Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible [Act cl. 3,4,5]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3,4,5]. Public buildings shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and any other facility that shall make them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 3,4,5]. answer_full:
Yes, public buildings are required to be accessible [Act cl. 3,4,5]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3,4,5]. Public buildings shall be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and any other facility that shall make them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 3,4,5].

From the date of the Act's commencement, there is a five-year transitory period during which all public buildings and structures, whether immovable, movable, or automobile, that were inaccessible to persons with disabilities shall be modified to be accessible and usable by persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 6,7] [Factsheet Section 6,7].

Before erecting any public structure, its plan shall be scrutinised by the relevant authority to ensure that the plan conforms with the building code [Act cl. 6,7] [Factsheet Section 7]. A government or government agency, body, or individual responsible for the approval of building plans shall not approve the plan of a public building if the plan does not make provision for accessibility facilities in line with the build [Act cl. 6,7]. Section 7(2) prohibits government bodies, agencies, or individuals responsible for the approval of building plans [Factsheet Section 7].

question: What employment protections exist for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29,30]. There is also a general mention of 5% of persons with disabilities in their employment [Factsheet general].
answer_full: All employers of labour in public organisations shall, as much as possible, have persons with disabilities constituting at least 5% of their employment [Act cl. 29,30]. There is also a general mention of 5% of persons with disabilities in their employment [Factsheet general].

question: Is there a commission for persons with disabilities?
answer_excerpt: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities. The Act provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Act general]. Specifically, there is established the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Act cl. 31]. This is also stated in Section 31 of the Factsheet, which establishes a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Factsheet Section 30,31].
answer_full: Yes, there is a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities. The Act provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Act general]. Specifically, there is established the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Act cl. 31]. This is also stated in Section 31 of the Factsheet, which establishes a National Commission for Persons with Disabilities [Factsheet Section 30,31].

question: Does the Act cover access to vehicles and transport?
answer_excerpt: Yes, the Act covers access to vehicles and transport. The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 10]. Every public vehicle shall have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years of commencement of this Act [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Transport service providers are mandated to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other access...
answer_full:
Yes, the Act covers access to vehicles and transport.

The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act mandates government providers to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids that enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 10]. Every public vehicle shall have functional audible and visual display of their destination within five years of commencement of this Act [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Transport service providers are mandated to make provisions for lifts, ramps and other accessibility facilities and aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Act cl. 11]. Lifts, ramps and all other accessibility equipment in or for vehicles, and at parks or bus stops, shall be maintained in operational condition [Act cl. 11]. Section 11 of the Act also mandates the regular and frequent maintenance of accessibility aids and equipment in vehicles [Factsheet Section 10,11]. Additionally, section 11(4) places a duty of care on a driver [Factsheet Section 10,11].

question: What rights do children with disabilities have to education?
answer_excerpt: Children with disabilities have several rights concerning education. A person with disability has an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 16,17]. This right includes free education up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17]. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities is mandated to provide educational assistive devices [Factsheet Section 17]. answer_full: Children with disabilities have several rights concerning education. A person with disability has an unfettered right to education without discrimination or segregation in any form [Act cl. 16,17]. This right includes free education up to secondary level [Factsheet Section 17]. The National Commission for Persons with Disabilities is mandated to provide educational assistive devices [Factsheet Section 17]. There is also a right to inclusiveness in education, as complemented by section 18 [Factsheet Section 19,17,20]. Furthermore, the government shall ensure that the education of persons with disabilities, particularly children who are blind, deaf, or with multiple disabilities, is delivered in the most appropriate language, mode, and means of communication for the individual, and in environments which maximise academic and social development [Act cl. 20]. Section 20 also provides for the education of persons with disabilities, especially children [Factsheet Section 19,17,20].

question: How long is the transitional compliance period?
answer_excerpt: The transitory period is five years [Factsheet Section 6,7].
answer_full: The transitory period is five years [Factsheet Section 6,7].

question: Does the Constitution guarantee dignity and equality?
answer_excerpt: Yes, the Constitution guarantees dignity and equality. The State social order is founded on ideals of Freedom, Equality and Justice [Constitution s. 17]. Every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17]. The sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17]. There is a Right to dignity of human persons [Constitution general].
answer_full:
Yes, the Constitution guarantees dignity and equality.

The State social order is founded on ideals of Freedom, Equality and Justice [Constitution s. 17]. Every citizen shall have equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law [Constitution s. 17]. The sanctity of the human person shall be recognised and human dignity shall [Constitution s. 17]. There is a Right to dignity of human persons [Constitution general].

question: Where can I get legal aid for a disability rights violation?
answer_excerpt: An indigent citizen of Nigeria can receive legal aid where their right under Chapter IV has been infringed or to enable them to engage the services of a legal practitioner to prosecute their claim [Constitution s. 46]. This legal aid is for ensuring that allegations of infringement of such rights are substantial and the requirement or need for financial or legal aid is real [Constitution s. 46]. The High Court has special jurisdiction and provides legal aid for these matters [Constitution s. 39].
answer_full: An indigent citizen of Nigeria can receive legal aid where their right under Chapter IV has been infringed or to enable them to engage the services of a legal practitioner to prosecute their claim [Constitution s. 46]. The High Court has special jurisdiction and provides legal aid for these matters [Constitution s. 39].
